title: Zionism and Racism
author: Hasan Sa'b
context: Published in January 1968 as Essay No. 2 by the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) Research Center in Beirut, this foundational monograph by Lebanese scholar and diplomat Dr. Hasan Sa'b provides an incisive critique of political Zionism as a racialist ideology, analyzing its roots in 19th-century European nationalist chauvinism and its settler-colonial practices of displacement and racial discrimination.
relatesToToday: Provides essential historical and conceptual foundations for understanding the institutionalized racial discrimination, ethnic segregation, and settler-colonial legal structures of the Israeli state, anticipating by seven years United Nations General Assembly Resolution 3379 which determined that Zionism is a form of racism and racial discrimination.
keyTakeaways: Traces the ideological genesis of political Zionism to European 19th-century racialist nationalism and colonial exclusivism.
Examines the historic Arab and Palestinian resistance against Zionist settler-colonial expansion and forced displacement.
Highlights the extensive tradition of universalist Jewish dissent against political Zionism, including critiques by Albert Einstein, Morris Cohen, and Judah Magnes.
Analyzes how the Zionist state structure enforces legal and economic discrimination against indigenous Palestinian citizens.

Exposes internal racial and ethnic hierarchies within Israel, specifically the systemic discrimination and cultural chauvinism directed by the Ashkenazi establishment against Sephardic and Mizrahi Jews.
Advocates for a democratic, secular, and anti-racial vision of coexistence across historic Palestine.
